<article class="devsite-article">
  
  
  
    <div class="devsite-banner devsite-banner-announcement nocontent" data-nosnippet
      
        
    background="orange"
  
      >
      <div class="devsite-banner-message">
        <div class="devsite-banner-message-text">
          <p><strong>Firebase Studio is sunsetting on March 22, 2027.</strong> As of June 22, 2026, new workspace creation and user signup are disabled. You can continue to work in and migrate your existing workspaces to Google AI Studio or Google Antigravity. <a href="/docs/studio/migrating-project">Learn how to migrate.</a></p> <p><em>Any apps already deployed to Firebase will continue to run even after the sunset date. Also, all our <u>core Firebase products</u> (like Firestore, Authentication, App Hosting, etc.) are <u>not impacted</u> by the Firebase Studio sunset.</em></p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
  
  

  <div class="devsite-article-meta nocontent" role="navigation" data-nosnippet>
    
    
    <ul class="devsite-breadcrumb-list"
  
    aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  
  <li class="devsite-breadcrumb-item
             ">
    
    
    
      
        
  <a href="https://firebase.google.com/"
      
        class="devsite-breadcrumb-link gc-analytics-event"
      
        data-category="Site-Wide Custom Events"
      
        data-label="Breadcrumbs"
      
        data-value="1"
      
        track-type="globalNav"
      
        track-name="breadcrumb"
      
        track-metadata-position="1"
      
        track-metadata-eventdetail="Firebase"

    <h1 class="devsite-page-title" tabindex="-1">
      Get started with the App Prototyping agent<devsite-actions hidden data-nosnippet><devsite-feature-tooltip
      ack-key="AckCollectionsBookmarkTooltipDismiss"
      analytics-category="Site-Wide Custom Events"
      analytics-action-show="Callout Profile displayed"
      analytics-action-close="Callout Profile dismissed"
      analytics-label="Create Collection Callout"
      class="devsite-page-bookmark-tooltip nocontent"
      data-nosnippet
      dismiss-button="true"
      id="devsite-collections-dropdown"
      
      dismiss-button-text="Dismiss"

      
      close-button-text="Got it">

    
    
      <devsite-bookmark></devsite-bookmark>
    

    <span slot="popout-heading">
      
      Stay organized with collections
    </span>
    <span slot="popout-contents">
      
      Save and categorize content based on your preferences.
    </span>
  </devsite-feature-tooltip>
    <devsite-llm-tools></devsite-llm-tools></devsite-actions>
  
      
    </h1>
  <div class="devsite-page-title-meta"><devsite-view-release-notes></devsite-view-release-notes></div>
  

  <devsite-toc class="devsite-nav"
    depth="2"
    devsite-toc-embedded
    >
  </devsite-toc>
  <div class="devsite-article-body clearfix
  ">

  
    
    

























































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































    























































<p></p>



<aside class="warning">
  <p><strong>Important:</strong> Creating new workspaces with the Prototyping
  agent is disabled as of June 22, 2026. To continue prototyping and building
  applications, we recommend migrating to Google AI Studio. For details, see the
  <a href="/docs/studio/migrating-project">migration guide</a>.</p>
</aside>

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> includes a web-based interface that lets you rapidly
prototype and generate AI-forward web apps using multimodal prompts, including
natural language, images, and drawing tools. The agent supports
Next.js apps, with other platforms and frameworks planned in the future.</p>

<p>The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> is a streamlined no-code development flow that
uses generative AI to develop, test, iterate, and publish a full-stack,
agentic web app. You describe your app idea in natural language with an
optional image, and
the agent generates an app blueprint, code, and a web preview. To
assist in the development and publishing of your full-stack app,
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> can automatically provision the following services for you:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>If your app uses AI:</strong> <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> adds the
<span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;Developer&nbsp;API</span> to your app, using the power of
<a href="https://genkit.dev/docs/flows/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> flows</a> to work with
<span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span>. You can use your own <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key or let
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> provision a Firebase project and <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key for
you.
</li>
<li><strong>If you want to publish your app to the web:</strong> <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> creates
a project and provides a quick way to publish your app with
<a href="/docs/app-hosting"><span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span></a>.</li>
</ul>
<aside class="special"><strong>Important:</strong><span> When the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> sets up the <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key
and other Firebase services, it creates a new Firebase project to
associate with the workspace. At this time, this is the only project that can
be associated when publishing from the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> view. Note that
you can publish to other Firebase projects by <a href="/docs/studio/github">checking your code into
GitHub</a> and <a href="/docs/app-hosting/get-started">creating an <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>
backend</a>. You can also use <a href="/docs/studio/google-integrations">Code
view</a> to integrate Firebase services.</span></aside>
<p>You can refine the app using natural language, images, and drawing tools,
edit code directly, roll back changes, publish the app,
and monitor its performance&mdash;all from <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> can help you build web apps with Next.js.</span></aside>
<h2 id="get-started" data-text="Get started" tabindex="-1">Get started</h2>

<p>To get started with the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, follow these steps:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Log into your Google Account and open
<a href="https://studio.firebase.google.com/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</p>

</li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Prototype an app with AI</strong> field, describe your app idea in
natural language.</p>



<p>For example, you could enter a prompt like the following to create a
recipe generation app:</p>


<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Text only"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Use secure coding practices to create an error-free web app that lets
users upload a photo or take a picture with their browser
camera. The app identifies the food in the picture and generates a
recipe and accompanying image that includes that food.

If no food product is identified, generate a random dessert recipe.
</code></pre></devsite-code>

<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> For best results, be as specific as possible in your prompt.
  Include the features you want, user workflows, and data requirements.
  Optionally, click <strong>Improve prompt</strong> to ask <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> to
  refine your initial prompt. Also understand that the most effective
  development processes with AI are iterative and you can continue to refine
  and add features collaboratively with <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span>. Learn more
  about crafting <a href="/docs/studio/prompting">effective prompts</a>.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>Optionally, upload an image to accompany your prompt. For example, you
can upload an image that contains the color scheme you want your app to
use and tell <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> to use it. Images must be less than 3 MiB.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Prototype with AI</strong>.</p>

<p>The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> generates an app blueprint based on your
prompt, returning a proposed app name, required features,

and style guidelines.
</p></li>
<li><p>Review the blueprint. If necessary, make a few changes. For example,
you could change the proposed app name or color scheme using one of
these options:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Click <span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">edit</span><strong>Customize</strong> and edit the
blueprint directly. Make your changes and click <strong>Save</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Describe...</strong> field in the chat pane, add clarifying questions
and context. You can also upload additional images.</p></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Prototype this app</strong>.</p>





<aside class="important"><p><b>Important:</b> <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> can
    generate output that seems plausible but is
    factually incorrect. It may respond with inaccurate information
    that doesn't represent Google's views. Validate all output from
    Gemini before you use it and do not use untested
    generated code in production. Do not enter personally-identifiable
    information (PII) or user data into the chat.</p>
</aside></li>
<li><p>The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> begins coding your app.</p>



<ul>
<li>If your
app uses AI, you&#39;re prompted to add or generate a
<a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key</a>.
If you click Auto-generate, the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> provisions a
Firebase project and a <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key for you.</li>
</ul>
<aside class="special"><strong>Important:</strong><span> If you choose <strong>Auto-generate</strong>, the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>
  creates a
  <a href="/docs/projects/learn-more">Firebase project</a> on your behalf with a
  prefix that matches the name of your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace
  and creates a new <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key in the project. It also stores
  the key within your
  <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace in an <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.env</code> file. To access your new
  project at any time, click the project name at the top of the page.
  To access your <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key to copy or delete in the future,
  use the
  <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials"><span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console</a>.</span></aside></li>
</ol>

<h2 id="iterate" data-text="Test, refine, debug, and iterate" tabindex="-1">Test, refine, debug, and iterate</h2>

<p>After the initial app is generated, you can test, refine, debug, and iterate.


<ul>
<li><p><strong>Review and interact with your app:</strong> After code generation completes,
a preview of your app appears. You can interact with the preview directly to
test it. Learn more at <a href="/docs/studio/preview-apps">Preview your app</a>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Add <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> and <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span>:</strong> During the iteration phase,
you can ask the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to add user authentication and a
database using <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> and <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span>. For example, give users
the ability to save and download recipes with a prompt like the following:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Text only"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">Add user authentication to the app. Authenticated users can:

  - Download the recipe and its generated image as a PDF (Print).

  - Save the recipe as public or private and make accessible to a search
    feature. For now, just save the text, not the image, to the database.

Important: Only authenticated users can download the PDF.
</code></pre></devsite-code><aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> can add <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> and
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span> to your app during the iteration phase, not in the initial
app blueprint.</span></aside></li>
<li><p><strong>Fix any errors as they occur:</strong> In most cases, the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>
prompts you to fix any errors that arise. Click <strong>Fix Error</strong> to allow
it to attempt a fix.</p>

<p>If you receive errors that you&#39;re not prompted to fix automatically,
copy the error and any relevant context (for example, &quot;Can you fix this
error in my Firebase initialization code?&quot;) into the chat window and
send it to <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span>.</p>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span> explains its reasoning, but you can also ask it to
     explain its plan before it executes it.</span></aside></li>
<li><p><strong>Test and iterate using natural language:</strong> Test your app thoroughly and
work with the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to iterate on the code and blueprint
until you&#39;re happy with it.</p>

<p>While in <span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> view, you can also use the following
features:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Click <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/annotate-icon.png" alt="Annotate icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Annotate</strong> to draw directly on the Preview window. Use the available
shape, image, and text tools, along with an optional text prompt, to
visually describe what you want the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to change.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/select-icon.png" alt="Select icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Select</strong> to select a specific element and enter instructions for
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>. This lets you quickly target a specific icon,
button, piece of text, or other element. When you click an image, you also
have the option of searching for and selecting a stock image from
<a href="https://unsplash.com" class="external">Unsplash</a>.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>Optionally, you can click <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-link.svg" alt="Link
icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Share preview link</strong> to share your app publicly and temporarily using
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> <a href="/docs/studio/preview-apps#share">public previews</a>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Create a Firebase project:</strong> The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> provisions a
<a href="/docs/projects/learn-more">Firebase project</a> on your behalf when you:</p>

<ul>
<li>Auto-generate a Gemini API key</li>
<li>Ask to connect your app to a Firebase project</li>
<li>Ask for help connecting your app to Firebase services, such as
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> or <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span></li>
<li>Click the <strong>Publish</strong> button and set up <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span></li>
</ul>

<p>To change the Firebase project connected to your workspace, prompt
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> with the project ID you want to use instead. For
example, &quot;Switch to Firebase project with ID <code translate="no" dir="ltr">&lt;your-project-id&gt;</code>.&quot;</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Test the app and verify <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> database rules:</strong> In the app
preview pane, upload an image that shows different foods to test your
app&#39;s ability to identify the ingredients and generate and save recipes.</p>

<p>Sign in as different users and generate recipes: make sure that
authenticated users can see their private recipes and recipes and that
all users see public recipes.</p>

<p>When you ask the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to add <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span>, it writes
and deploys <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span> database rules for you. Review the rules in the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/firestore/databases/-default-/rules" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</a>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Debug and iterate directly in the code:</strong> Click <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch
icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Switch to Code</strong> to open <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view, where you can see
all of your app&#39;s files and modify your code directly. You can switch back
to <span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> mode at any time.</p>

<p>While in <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view, you can also use the following
helpful features:</p>

<ul>
<li><p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span>&#39;s
<a href="/docs/studio/debug">built-in debugging and reporting features</a> to
inspect, debug, and audit your app.</p></li>
<li><p><a href="/docs/studio/try-gemini">AI assistance using <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span></a>
either inline within your code or using <span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> interactive chat
(both are available by default). Interactive chat can
diagnose issues, provide solutions, and run tools to help fix your app
faster.
To access chat, click
<span class="google-symbols">spark</span><strong><span class="notranslate">Gemini</span></strong>
at the bottom of the workspace.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span>


Apps created with the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> default to
the <span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> chat in <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view. To use
<span class="notranslate">Gemini</span> interactive chat instead, under
<strong><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span></strong>, click <strong>+</strong>, then select
<strong>New Chat</strong>. To
return to <span class="notranslate">Prototyper</span> chat, click
<span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">history</span> <strong>Recent chats</strong>, and
then choose <strong>Prototyper chat</strong>.</span></aside></li>
<li><p><a href="/docs/emulator-suite">Access the <span class="notranslate">Firebase Local Emulator Suite</span> to view database and
authentication data</a>. To open the emulator in
your workspace:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Click <img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch
icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Switch to Code</strong> and open the <strong><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></strong> extension
(<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ctrl+&#39;,Ctrl+&#39;</code>, or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Cmd+&#39;,Cmd+&#39;</code> on MacOS).</p></li>
<li><p>Scroll to <strong>Backend ports</strong> and expand it.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Actions</strong> column that corresponds to <strong>Port 4000</strong>, click
<strong>Open in new window</strong>.</p></li>
</ol></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p><strong>Test and measure your generative AI feature performance:</strong> You can use
the <span class="notranslate">Genkit Developer UI</span> to run your <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> AI flows, test, debug,
interact with different models, refine your prompts, and more.</p>

<p>To load your <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> flows in the <span class="notranslate">Genkit Developer UI</span> and start
testing:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>From the terminal in your <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> workspace, run the
following command to source your <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key and start the
<span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> server:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Bash"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>npm<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>run<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>genkit:watch
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>Click the <span class="notranslate">Genkit Developer UI</span> link. The <span class="notranslate">Genkit Developer UI</span>
opens in a new window with your flows, prompts, embedders, and a
selection of different available models.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Learn more about the <span class="notranslate">Genkit Developer UI</span> at
<a href="https://genkit.dev/docs/devtools/" class="external">Genkit Developer Tools</a>.</p></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="app-hosting" data-text="Publish your app with Firebase App Hosting" tabindex="-1">Publish your app with <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span></h2>

<p>After you&#39;ve tested your app and are satisfied with it in your workspace,
you can publish it to the web with
<a href="/docs/app-hosting"><span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span></a>.</p>

<aside class="caution"><strong>Important:</strong> <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span>
  requires a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account. When you link a billing account to a
  Firebase project, then your project is automatically upgraded to the
  <a href="/pricing">pay-as-you-go Blaze pricing plan</a> and your
  <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> and
  other Firebase and Google Cloud service usage is upgraded to the paid
  tier. You will be charged for usage of paid services that exceed the
  no-cost quota. Learn more at <a href="/docs/app-hosting/costs">Understand
  <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> costs</a>, <a href="/pricing">Firebase pricing</a>, and
  <a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing"
     class="external"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span> Developer API pricing</a>.
</aside>

<p>When you set up <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>, <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> creates a
<a href="/docs/studio/firebase-projects">Firebase project</a>
for you (if one was not already created by auto-generating a <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key
or other backend services)
and guides you through linking a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account.</p>

</span></aside>
<p>To publish your app:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Click <strong>Publish</strong> to set up your
<a href="/docs/studio/firebase-projects">Firebase project</a> and publish your app.
The <strong>Publish your app</strong> pane appears.</p>
<aside class="special"><strong>Important:</strong><span> If you did not <a href="/docs/studio/get-started-ai#get-started">auto-generate a <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span>
key</a> or prompt
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> to create a Firebase project,
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> provisions a <a href="/docs/studio/firebase-projects">Firebase
project</a> on your
behalf when you click <strong>Publish</strong>. You can access the Firebase project by
clicking the project name at the top of the page.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Firebase project</strong> step, the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> displays the
Firebase project associated with the workspace. If a Firebase project
doesn&#39;t already exist, the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> creates a new project for
you. Click <strong>Next</strong> to proceed.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Link <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account</strong> step, choose one of the following:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>Select the <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account that you want to link to your Firebase
project.</p></li>
<li><p>If you don&#39;t have a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account or want to create a new one,
click <strong>Create a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account</strong>. This opens the
<span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console, where you can <a href="https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/create-billing-account">create a new self-serve
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span>
account</a>.
After you create the account, return to <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> and select
the account from the <strong>Link <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span></strong> list.</p></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Next</strong>. <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> links the billing account to the project
associated with your workspace, created either when you auto-generated a
<span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> key or when you clicked <strong>Publish</strong>.</p>

<aside class="caution"><strong>Important:</strong> <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Hosting</span>
  requires a <span class="notranslate">Cloud Billing</span> account. When you link a billing account to a
  Firebase project, then your project is automatically upgraded to the
  <a href="/pricing">pay-as-you-go Blaze pricing plan</a> and your
  <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini&nbsp;API</span> and
  other Firebase and Google Cloud service usage is upgraded to the paid
  tier. You will be charged for usage of paid services that exceed the
  no-cost quota. Learn more at <a href="/docs/app-hosting/costs">Understand
  <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> costs</a>, <a href="/pricing">Firebase pricing</a>, and
  <a href="https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing"
     class="external"><span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span> Developer API pricing</a>.
</aside></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Set up services</strong>. The <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span> begins
provisioning Firebase services.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Publish now</strong>. <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> sets up Firebase services
and then launches the <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> rollout. This can take up to several
minutes to complete.
To learn more about what&#39;s happening behind the scenes, see
<a href="/docs/app-hosting/build">The <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> build process</a>.</p>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> If you don&#39;t want to publish now, you can click <strong>Publish later</strong>.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>When the publish step completes, the <strong>App overview</strong> appears with a
URL and app insights powered by <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> observability. To use a
custom domain (like example.com or app.example.com) instead of the
Firebase-generated domain, you can <a href="/docs/app-hosting/custom-domain">add a custom
domain</a> in the <span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console.</p></li>
</ol>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> If you receive any errors during publishing, see <a href="/docs/studio/troubleshooting#failed-to-publish">I received a &quot;Failed to
publish app&quot; error after
publishing</a> for instructions
on how to find and fix publishing errors.</span></aside>
<p>For more information about <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>, see
<a href="/docs/app-hosting/about-app-hosting">Understand <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> and how it
works</a>.</p>

<h2 id="app-check" data-text="Secure your app with Firebase App Check and reCAPTCHA Enterprise" tabindex="-1">Secure your app with <span class="notranslate">Firebase App Check</span> and reCAPTCHA Enterprise</h2>

<p>If you&#39;ve integrated Firebase or Google Cloud services into your app,
<span class="notranslate">Firebase App Check</span> helps protect your app backends from abuse by preventing
unauthorized clients from accessing your Firebase resources. It works with
both Google services (including Firebase and Google Cloud services) and
your own custom backends to keep your resources safe.</p>

<p>We recommend adding <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> to any app you post publicly to protect your
backend resources from abuse.</p>

<p>This section guides you through setting up <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> within
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> using <a href="/docs/app-check/web/recaptcha-enterprise-provider">reCAPTCHA
Enterprise</a> for a web app
created by the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, but you can set up <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> within
any app that implements Firebase services and can implement custom providers.
Learn more at <a href="/docs/app-check"><span class="notranslate">Firebase App Check</span></a>.</p>

<p>ReCAPTCHA Enterprise provides <a href="https://cloud.google.com/recaptcha/docs/compare-tiers">up to 10,000 assessments at
no-cost</a>.</p>

<h3 id="set-up-recaptcha" data-text="Step 1: Set up reCAPTCHA Enterprise for your app" tabindex="-1">Step 1: Set up reCAPTCHA Enterprise for your app</h3>

<ol>
<li><p>Open the <a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/security/recaptcha?project=_">reCAPTCHA Enterprise</a>
section of the <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the name of your Firebase project from the <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console
project picker.</p></li>
<li><p>If you&#39;re prompted to enable the reCAPTCHA Enterprise API, do so.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Get started</strong>, and add a <strong>Display name</strong> for your reCAPTCHA
site key.</p></li>
<li><p>Accept the default <strong>Web</strong> <strong>Application type</strong> key.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Add a domain</strong> and add a domain. You&#39;ll want to add your
<span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> domain (for example,
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">studio--<var translate="no">PROJECT_ID</var>.<var translate="no">REGION</var>.hosted.app</code>)
and any custom domains you use with or plan to use with your app.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Next step</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Leave <strong>Will you use challenges?</strong> unselected.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Create key</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Copy and save your <strong>Key ID</strong> and proceed to <a href="#configure-app-check"><strong>Configure <span class="notranslate">App Check</span></strong></a>.</p></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="configure-app-check" data-text="Step 2: Configure App Check" tabindex="-1">Step 2: Configure <span class="notranslate">App Check</span></h3>

<ol>
<li><p>Open the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/appcheck" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</a> 
and click <strong>Build</strong> &gt; <strong>App Check</strong> from the navigation menu.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Get started</strong>, then click <strong>Register</strong> next to your app.</p></li>
<li><p>Click to expand <strong>ReCAPTCHA</strong> and paste the Key ID you generated for
reCAPTCHA Enterprise.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="add-app-check-to-code" data-text="Step 3: Add App Check to your code" tabindex="-1">Step 3: Add <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> to your code</h3>

<ol>
<li><p>Return to <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> and in <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view, add
the site key you generated to your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.env</code> file:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Text only"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=<var translate="no">RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY</var>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>If you don&#39;t already have your Firebase configuration saved to <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.env</code>,
obtain it:</p>

<ul>
<li><p>From the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/settings"><span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</a>,
open <strong>Project settings</strong> and locate it within your the section that
corresponds with your app.</p></li>
<li><p>From the Terminal in <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view:</p>

<ol>
<li>Log into Firebase: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">firebase auth login</code></li>
<li>Select your project:
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">firebase use <var translate="no">FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID</var></code></li>
<li>Obtain the Firebase config: <code translate="no" dir="ltr">firebase apps:sdkconfig</code></li>
</ol></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Add the configuration to your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">.env</code> file so that it looks like the
following:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Text only"><code translate="no" dir="ltr">NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=<var translate="no">FIREBASE_API_KEY</var>
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=<var translate="no">FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN</var>
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=<var translate="no">FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID</var>
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=<var translate="no">FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET</var>
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=<var translate="no">FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID</var>
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=<var translate="no">FIREBASE_APP_ID</var>
NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY=<var translate="no">RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY</var>
</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>Add <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> to your app code. You can ask <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span> to add
<span class="notranslate">App Check</span> with reCAPTCHA Enterprise to your app (be sure to
specify &quot;reCAPTCHA Enterprise&quot; and be sure to double-check it!), or
follow the steps in <a href="/docs/app-check/web/recaptcha-enterprise-provider#initialize">Initialize
<span class="notranslate">App Check</span></a>.</p></li>
<li><p>Re-publish your site to <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>. Try testing your
database and authentication features to generate some data.</p></li>
<li><p>Verify that <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> is receiving requests in the
<span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console by opening <strong>Build</strong> &gt; <strong>App Check</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Click to inspect <span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span>. After you verify that requests arrive,
click <strong>Enforce</strong> to enforce <span class="notranslate">App Check</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>Repeat verification and enforcement for <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span>.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>If, after you have registered your app for <span class="notranslate">App Check</span>, you want to run your
app in an environment that <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> would normally not classify as valid,
such as locally during development, or from a continuous integration (CI)
environment, you can create a debug build of your app that uses the
<span class="notranslate">App Check</span> debug provider instead of a real attestation provider. Learn more
at <a href="/docs/app-check/web/debug-provider">Use <span class="notranslate">App Check</span> with the debug provider in web
apps</a>.</p>

<h2 id="monitor-your-app" data-text="Monitor your app" tabindex="-1">Monitor your app</h2>

<p>The <strong>App overview</strong> panel in <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> provides key
metrics and information about your app, letting you monitor your web app&#39;s
performance using <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>&#39;s built-in observability tools. After your
site rolls out, you can access the overview by clicking <strong>Publish</strong>. From this
panel, you can:</p>

<ul>
<li>Click <strong>Publish</strong> to release a new version of your app.</li>
<li>Share the link to your app or open your app directly in
<strong>Visit your app</strong>.</li>
<li>Review a summary of your app&#39;s performance over the last 7 days,
including the total number of requests and the status of your latest
rollout. Click <strong>View details</strong> to access even more information in the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/apphosting/" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</a>.</li>
<li>View a graph of the number of the number of requests your app has
received over the last 24 hours, broken down by HTTP status code.</li>
<li>View the activation status of Firebase services like <span class="notranslate">Firebase Authentication</span> and
<span class="notranslate">Cloud Firestore</span>.</li>
</ul>

<p>If you close the App overview panel, you can re-open it at any time by
clicking <strong>Publish</strong>.</p>

<p>Learn more about managing and monitoring <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> rollouts at
<a href="/docs/app-hosting/rollouts">Manage rollouts and releases</a>.</p>

<h2 id="roll-back" data-text="Roll back your deployment" tabindex="-1">Roll back your deployment</h2>

<p>If you&#39;ve deployed successive versions of your app to <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>, you can
roll it back to one of the earlier versions. You can also remove it.</p>

<ul>
<li><p>To roll back a published site:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>Open <a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/apphosting" class="external"><span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> in the
<span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>Locate your app&#39;s backend, click <strong>View</strong>, and then click <strong>Rollouts</strong>.</p></li>
<li><p>Next to the deployment you want to roll back to, click <strong>More</strong>
<span class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">more_vert</span>, then choose <strong>Roll
back to this build</strong>, and confirm.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>Learn more at <a href="/docs/app-hosting/rollouts">Manage rollouts and releases</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>To remove your <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> domain from the web:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>From the
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/apphosting" class="external"><span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</a>,
open <strong><span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span></strong>, and click <strong>View</strong> in the
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> app section.</p></li>
<li><p>In the <strong>Backend information</strong> section, click <strong>Manage</strong>. The
<strong>Domains</strong> page loads.</p></li>
<li><p>Next to your domain, click <strong>More</strong> <span
class="material-icons" aria-hidden="true" translate="no">more_vert</span>, then choose <strong>Disable domain</strong>,
and confirm.</p></li>
</ol>

<p>This removes your domain from the web. To fully remove your
<span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> backend, follow the instructions in <a href="/docs/app-hosting/configure#delete-backend">Delete a
backend</a>.</p></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="genkit-monitoring" data-text="Use Genkit monitoring for your deployed features" tabindex="-1">Use <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> monitoring for your deployed features</h2>

<p>You can monitor your <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> feature steps, inputs, and outputs by enabling
telemetry to your AI flow code. The telemetry feature for <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> lets you
monitor the performance and usage of your AI flows. This data can help you
identify areas for improvement, troubleshoot issues, optimize your prompts and
flows for better performance and cost efficiency, and track the usage of your
flows over time.</p>

<p>To set up monitoring in <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span>, you add telemetry to the <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> AI flows
and then view the results in the <span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console.</p>
<aside class="special"><strong>Important:</strong><span> <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> monitoring relies on telemetry data written to
Google Cloud Logging, Metrics, and Trace, which are paid services. View the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/pricing" class="external">Google Cloud Observability pricing</a> 
page for pricing details and to learn about free-of-charge tier limits.</span></aside>
<h3 id="add-telemetry" data-text="Step 1: Add telemetry to your Genkit flow code in Firebase Studio" tabindex="-1">Step 1: Add telemetry to your <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> flow code in <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></h3>

<p>To set up monitoring in your code:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>If you aren&#39;t already in <span class="notranslate">Code</span> view, click
<img src="/static/docs/studio/images/icons/codicon-code.svg" alt="Code switch
icon" class="inline-icon"> 
<strong>Switch to Code</strong> to open it.</p></li>
<li><p>Check <code translate="no" dir="ltr">package.json</code> to verify the version of <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> that&#39;s installed.</p></li>
<li><p>Open the terminal (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">Ctrl-Shift-C</code>, or <code translate="no" dir="ltr">Cmd-Shift-C</code> in MacOS).</p></li>
<li><p>Click inside the terminal and install the Firebase plugin, using the
version that matches your <code translate="no" dir="ltr">package.json</code> file. For example, if the
<span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> packages in your
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">package.json</code> are at 1.0.4, you should run the following command to
install the plugin:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Bash"><code class="devsite-terminal" translate="no" dir="ltr">npm<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>i<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>--save<span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span>@genkit-ai/firebase@1.0.4</code></pre></devsite-code></li>
<li><p>From <strong>Explorer</strong>, expand <code translate="no" dir="ltr">src &gt; ai &gt; flows</code>. One or more TypeScript files
that contain your <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> flows appear in the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">flows</code> folder.</p></li>
<li><p>Click one of the flows to open it.</p>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> Note the <code translate="no" dir="ltr">prompt</code> section of the file: You can edit this manually to
refine <span class=\"notranslate\">Gemini</span>&#39;s responses.</span></aside></li>
<li><p>At the bottom of the imports section of the file, add the following to
import and enable <code translate="no" dir="ltr">FirebaseTelemetry</code>:</p>
<div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="TypeScript"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-k">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">enableFirebaseTelemetry</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'@genkit-ai/firebase'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-nx">enableFirebaseTelemetry</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">();</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code><aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> To learn more about advanced telemetry options in <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span>, see
<a href="https://genkit.dev/docs/js/observability/advanced-configuration/#default-configuration" class="external">Advanced configuration</a>.</span></aside></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="set-permissions" data-text="Step 2: Set up permissions" tabindex="-1">Step 2: Set up permissions</h3>

<p><span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span> enabled the
<a href="https://genkit.dev/docs/js/observability/getting-started/#step-2-enable-the-required-apis" class="external">required APIs</a> 
for you when it set up your Firebase project, but you also need to provide
permissions to the <span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span> service account.</p>

<p>To set up permissions:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>In the <span class="notranslate">Google Cloud</span> console, go to the
<a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/iam" class="external"><strong>IAM</strong> page</a> and
select your Firebase project.</p></li>
<li><p>Grant the following roles to the <strong>App Hosting service account</strong>:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Monitoring Metric Writer</strong> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">roles/monitoring.metricWriter</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Cloud Trace Agent</strong> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">roles/cloudtrace.agent</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Logs Writer</strong> (<code translate="no" dir="ltr">roles/logging.logWriter</code>)</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p><a href="/docs/studio/deploy-app#app-hosting">Re-publish your app</a> to
<span class="notranslate">App Hosting</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>When publishing is complete, load your app and start using it. After five
minutes, your app should start logging telemetry data.</p></li>
</ol>

<h3 id="monitor-genkit" data-text="Step 3: Monitor your generative AI features on the Firebase console" tabindex="-1">Step 3: Monitor your generative AI features on the <span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console</h3>

<p>When telemetry is configured, <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> records the number of requests,
success, and latency for all of your flows, and, for each specific flow,
<span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> collects stability metrics, shows detailed graphs, and logs
captured traces.</p>

<p>To monitor your AI features implemented with <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span>:</p>

<ol>
<li><p>After five minutes, in the <span class="notranslate">Firebase</span> console, go to <strong>AI Services</strong> &gt;
<a href="https://console.firebase.google.com/project/_/genkit" class="external">Genkit</a> to
review prompts and responses from <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>You can review the following <strong>Stability metrics</strong> compiled by <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span>:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Total requests:</strong> The total number of requests received by your flow.</li>
<li><strong>Success rate:</strong> The percentage of requests that were successfully
processed.</li>
<li><strong>95th percentile latency:</strong> The 95th percentile latency of your flow,
which is the time it takes for 95% of requests to be processed.</li>
<li><p><strong>Token usage:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li>Input tokens: The number of tokens sent to the model in the prompt.</li>
<li>Output tokens: The number of tokens generated by the model in the
response.</li>
</ul></li>
<li><p><strong>Image usage:</strong></p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Input images:</strong> The number of images sent to the model in the prompt.</li>
<li><strong>Output images:</strong> The number of images generated by the model in the
response.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>You can expand stability metrics to view the following detailed graphs:</p>

<ul>
<li>Request volume over time.</li>
<li>Success rate over time.</li>
<li>Input and output tokens over time.</li>
<li>Latency (95th and 50th percentile) over time.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>

<p>Learn more about <span class="notranslate">Genkit</span> in their
<a href="https://genkit.dev/" class="external">documentation</a>.</p>
<aside class="tip"><strong>Tip:</strong><span> For a guided tour of the full application lifecycle with
the <span class="notranslate">App Prototyping agent</span>, from inception through monitoring your
published web app, check out <a href="/docs/studio/solution-build-with-ai">Develop, publish, and monitor a full-stack web
app with <span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</span></aside>
<h2 id="next-steps" data-text="Next steps" tabindex="-1">Next steps</h2>

<ul>
<li><a href="/docs/studio/solution-build-with-ai">Develop, publish, and monitor a full-stack web app with
<span class="notranslate">Firebase Studio</span></a>.</li>
<li><a href="/docs/studio/get-started-template">Develop applications with any framework with a template or
solution</a>.</li>
</ul>
